name: Soccer Stories FR
_comment_group: Another show under the Snapchat heading, and the same kind of thing
every one of them is: the heading names the network these frames are
cut FOR and the channel is the show they are cut from, so another show
cutting for the same network is one more folder under it rather than a
heading of its own.
Like all of its neighbours it is a frame fetcher rather than a
thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of vertical
stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said over it.
It is the fourth of the packs set in League Spartan, and
dr-football-us is the one to read: this pack's face, its two-question
palette and its absent highlight are all that pack's, argued there at
length, and the argument is about the FACE rather than about either
show. Behind that sits Hall of Femme, whose design all four are cut
to.
The FR in the name is the account's, and it says which of the brand's
feeds this is rather than what language the app is in. What arrives on
the frames is whatever the video's own voice track was saying, put
through the transcription and the rewrite exactly as it is on every
channel here; nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the
app itself says is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
What this pack decides is its two colours - and it is the one of the
four whose type is black rather than white, which is the card's doing
and is argued under `color`.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Set in League Spartan on a warm vermilion card, in two colours the
user picks per frame. Everything else about how the words are set -
the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the shape of the card,
where it stands on the frame - is the Snapchat caption design and is
Why League Spartan suits a caption at this size, and why its single
cut leaves this channel with no highlight, is written out in
dr-football-us. Nothing about it is different here.

_comment_color: The channel's own answer, and therefore what every frame is set in
until somebody presses a swatch: a frame stores no colour of its
own until it is given one, and this is what it falls back to (see
state.textColorFor). It is one of the two in `colors` below, so
the black swatch is the one that shows as chosen on an untouched
frame - the swatch is found by matching this value rather than by
being listed first.
Black, where the other three League Spartan packs open on white,
and it is the CARD that decides which. #474A92 and #312ED5 are
dark blues and white is the only thing that reads on them;
#EB523A is a light warm red, and white on it is the pairing that
looks strong on a monitor and turns into a caption with no edges
on a phone at arm's length. Black on it is unambiguous at every
size and over every still underneath.
Absolute black rather than a soft near-black, for the reason the
other packs give for absolute white: on a saturated card an
off-black picks the card's colour up and reads as a caption
printed out of register rather than as a softer black. There is
nothing for a true black to be too harsh against either - it is on
a colour somebody chose, not on a photograph.
_comment_colors: The two colours this show is set in, offered for the letters and
for the card behind them - two buttons in each of the two rows in
The same shape of palette dr-football-us has, and for the same
reasons, written out there: one brand colour and one absolute,
offered as the pairing and its inverse; the same list twice
because what is on offer is the pairing rather than two unrelated
sets; and two rows and not three, because there is no highlight
_comment_highlight: None. Every line of every caption on this channel is set the same
way, and the highlight buttons stand where they stand everywhere
else and go dead with a tooltip saying whose decision that was.
dr-football-us is where this is argued: the app carries one cut of
League Spartan, so the change of CUT every sibling picks its words
out with is not available, a synthesised weight would be measured
as well as drawn, and a recolour into the palette's other colour
is the card's own colour. A pack in that position says it has no
highlight rather than shipping one nobody could tell apart from
_comment_panel: Vermilion, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
It is the first entry in `colors.panel` above as well, so the
swatch that shows as chosen on an untouched frame is the one at
the start of the row - though nothing requires that, since the
swatch is found by matching this value rather than by being listed

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it
is on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved.
